sections.subtitle: Život u dva dijela: bez Boga i s Bogom
sections.screenshot_description: Goran Ćurković pred publikom najavljuje da se njegova životna priča sastoji od dva dijela
sections.content:
Goran Ćurković svjedočanstvo otvara pozdravom „Hvaljen Isus i Marija, braćo i sestre u Kristu“ i pomalo šaljivim priznanjem: **ljubomoran je na mlade slušatelje** jer su relativno brzo došli do vjere. Sam se, kaže, „morao malo napatiti“, ali dodaje da svatko ima svoj put.

Najavljuje da će ispričati životnu priču koja se sastoji od dva dijela: **prvi bez Boga, drugi s Bogom**. Koji je bolji, ostavlja slušateljima da sami procijene.

Rođen je u Splitu, u katoličkoj obitelji, no u kući nije bilo ni molitve, ni vjere, ni odlaska u crkvu. Roditelji su od njega tražili da ide u crkvu, a on je odbijao jer je gledao njihov primjer: „Ne idete vi, zašto moram ja?“ Otac, kojeg opisuje kao teškog čovjeka, ipak ga je natjerao na vjeronauk.

U crkvi mu je bilo dosadno. Deset Božjih zapovijedi doživljavao je kao popis zabrana: ne smiješ krasti, lagati, psovati ni hodati s tuđim ženama. Zaključio je da je to život „za jednu staru baku koja treba brzo umrijeti“ i da mu ostaje još samo molitva. Bio je uvjeren da u crkvi **nije dobio ništa**.
sections.subtitle_en: Life in Two Parts: Without God and With God
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran Ćurković announces before the audience that his life story consists of two parts
sections.content_en:
Goran Ćurković opens his testimony with the greeting "Praised be Jesus and Mary, brothers and sisters in Christ" and a somewhat humorous admission: **he is jealous of the young listeners** because they arrived at faith relatively quickly. He himself, he says, "had to suffer a bit," but adds that everyone has their own path.

He announces that he will tell a life story that consists of two parts: **the first without God, the second with God**. Which one is better, he leaves to the listeners to judge for themselves.

He was born in Split, into a Catholic family, but in the house there was neither prayer, nor faith, nor going to church. His parents demanded that he go to church, and he refused because he watched their example: "You don't go, why do I have to?" His father, whom he describes as a difficult man, nevertheless forced him to attend catechism.

He was bored in church. He experienced the Ten Commandments as a list of prohibitions: you must not steal, lie, curse, or run around with other men's wives. He concluded that this was a life "for an old grandma who needs to die soon" and that the only thing left for him was prayer. He was convinced that in church **he received nothing**.

sections.subtitle: Dom obilježen tragedijom i dječak koji je htio biti „frajer“
sections.screenshot_description: Goran opisuje svoje filmske idole iz američkih akcijskih filmova
sections.content:
Obitelj Ćurković pogodilo je nekoliko teških tragedija. Goranova sestra s četiri je godine **pala s petog kata i poginula**, pred majčinim nogama. Brat je s godinu dana obolio od meningitisa i ostao gluhonijem. Majka je stalno plakala i bila depresivna, a budući da u kući nije bilo Boga, počela je piti. Goran o njoj govori sa sućuti: „Jadnica, mislila da s alkoholom će riješiti boli koje je nosila u srcu.“ Otac je bio pomorac, više na brodu nego kod kuće.

Goran je odrastao na ulici ili pred televizorom. Obožavao je američke akcijske filmove, a njihovi glumci postali su mu idoli. Bili su lijepi i tetovirani, imali su velike mišiće, tukli su se i sjedili po zatvorima, a uz to su imali lijepe žene, dobre automobile i puno novca, pušili su Marlboro i pili viski. Iz toga je složio jednostavnu sliku: **muškarac treba biti frajer**.

S deset godina počeo je pušiti i piti alkohol. S jedanaest je bio siguran da zna sve o životu. Dosadili su mu škola, obitelj i svi koji su mu govorili kako se treba ponašati. Zaključio je da je dovoljno velik da živi sam, pa je pobjegao od kuće u drugi grad. Ondje je opljačkao dućan, a policija ga je uhvatila i zatvorila.
sections.subtitle_en: A Home Marked by Tragedy and a Boy Who Wanted to Be a "Tough Guy"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran describes his movie idols from American action films
sections.content_en:
The Ćurković family was struck by several severe tragedies. Goran's sister, at four years old, **fell from the fifth floor and died**, at their mother's feet. His brother contracted meningitis at one year old and remained deaf-mute. His mother cried constantly and was depressed, and since there was no God in the house, she began to drink. Goran speaks of her with compassion: "Poor thing, she thought that with alcohol she would resolve the pains she carried in her heart." His father was a sailor, more on the ship than at home.

Goran grew up on the street or in front of the television. He adored American action films, and their actors became his idols. They were handsome and tattooed, had big muscles, fought and sat in prisons, and in addition they had beautiful women, nice cars, and lots of money, smoked Marlboro, and drank whiskey. From that he put together a simple picture: **a man needs to be a tough guy**.

At ten years old he began smoking and drinking alcohol. At eleven he was sure he knew everything about life. He grew tired of school, family, and everyone who told him how he should behave. He concluded that he was big enough to live on his own, so he ran away from home to another city. There he robbed a shop, and the police caught him and locked him up.

sections.subtitle: Otac koji nije znao razgovarati, samo tući
sections.screenshot_description: Goran govori o odnosu s ocem u kojem nikad nije bilo razgovora
sections.content:
Policija je odmah pozvala oca da dođe po sina, no otac ga je **ostavio tri dana** u pritvoru. Goran objašnjava da je otac razmišljao logično: ako sin ostane koji dan duže, uplašit će se i promijeniti.

Za odnos s ocem kaže da ne zna može li ga se uopće tako nazvati. Ističe da mu je otac dobar čovjek, ali s jednim velikim problemom: **nije znao komunicirati**. U kući nikad nije bilo razgovora, a cijeli odgoj svodio se na batine. Otac je vjerovao da će batinama riješiti sve probleme.

Kad je nakon tri dana došao po njega, ništa ga nije pitao. Odmah ga je pretukao u policijskoj stanici, i to toliko da je **policija morala braniti dječaka od vlastitog oca**. Tukao ga je zatim još dva i pol sata u autobusu na putu kući.
sections.subtitle_en: A Father Who Did Not Know How to Talk, Only How to Beat
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran speaks about the relationship with his father in which there was never any conversation
sections.content_en:
The police immediately called his father to come get his son, but his father **left him for three days** in custody. Goran explains that his father thought logically: if the son stays a few days longer, he will get scared and change.

About the relationship with his father, he says he does not know whether it can be called that at all. He emphasizes that his father is a good man, but with one big problem: **he did not know how to communicate**. In the house there was never any conversation, and his entire upbringing came down to beatings. His father believed that he would solve all problems with beatings.

When he came to get him after three days, he asked him nothing. He beat him immediately in the police station, and that so severely that **the police had to defend the boy from his own father**. He then beat him for another two and a half hours on the bus on the way home.

sections.subtitle: Majčina smrt, mržnja i metak na prvu godišnjicu
sections.screenshot_description: Goran prepričava datum 2. lipnja 1978. i pokušaj samoubojstva pištoljem
sections.content:
Kad je Goranu bilo trinaest godina, umrla mu je majka. Zapao je u depresiju jer je nikad nije zagrlio ni poljubio i nikad joj nije rekao da je voli. A volio ju je i bezbroj puta poželio pokazati tu ljubav. Nije mogao jer je vjerovao da **muškarac ne smije pokazivati osjećaje** i da su osjećaji za žene. Ta ga je bol dovela do odluke da se ubije.

Osam mjeseci nakon majčine smrti otac se ponovno oženio. Tada se u Goranu **prvi put javila mržnja** prema ocu jer nije mogao shvatiti kako je nakon osam mjeseci „zaboravio“ njegovu majku. Mrzio je i brata, kojemu je, kako je tada mislio, sve bilo svejedno i koji je i sam postao alkoholičar. Mrzio je i ženu koja je, po njegovim riječima, došla „glumiti majku“.

Na **2. lipnja 1978.**, prvu godišnjicu majčine smrti, posudio je pištolj od prijatelja. Otac je kod kuće gledao Svjetsko nogometno prvenstvo u Argentini. Goran je sjeo blizu njega jer je htio razgovarati, no otac se nervozno okrenuo, udario ga i potjerao u sobu. U sobi je uzeo pištolj i pucao sebi u glavu.

Probudio se u bolnici i čuo liječnika kako govori da operacija nije uspjela: **metak je ostao u glavi**, ne može se izvaditi, Goran neće dugo živjeti i imat će velikih problema s glavom. Nekoliko dana kasnije otac i maćeha rekli su mu da je sve u redu i da je metak izvađen. Njemu je bilo svejedno. Zapao je u još dublju depresiju jer se nije uspio ubiti.
sections.subtitle_en: Mother's Death, Hatred, and a Bullet on the First Anniversary
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran recounts the date of June 2, 1978, and the suicide attempt with a gun
sections.content_en:
When Goran was thirteen years old, his mother died. He fell into depression because he had never hugged or kissed her and had never told her that he loved her. And he loved her and countless times wished to show that love. He could not because he believed that **a man must not show feelings** and that feelings are for women. That pain brought him to the decision to kill himself.

Eight months after his mother's death, his father remarried. At that point, in Goran **for the first time hatred arose** toward his father because he could not understand how after eight months he had "forgotten" his mother. He also hated his brother, to whom, as he thought then, nothing mattered and who also became an alcoholic himself. He also hated the woman who, in his words, came to "act like a mother."

On **June 2, 1978**, the first anniversary of his mother's death, he borrowed a gun from a friend. His father was at home watching the World Cup in Argentina. Goran sat down near him because he wanted to talk, but his father turned around nervously, hit him, and chased him into his room. In the room, he took the gun and shot himself in the head.

He woke up in the hospital and heard the doctor saying that the surgery had not succeeded: **the bullet remained in his head**, it could not be removed, Goran would not live long and would have major problems with his head. A few days later, his father and stepmother told him that everything was fine and that the bullet had been removed. To him it was all the same. He fell into an even deeper depression because he had not succeeded in killing himself.

sections.subtitle: „Bezopasna“ trava, epilepsija i heroin
sections.screenshot_description: Goran ironično prepričava kako su ga prijatelji nagovarali na marihuanu
sections.content:
Nakon izlaska iz bolnice Goran je uz alkohol počeo uzimati i tablete. Uvijek se družio sa starijima, a oni su već dugo pušili marihuanu i hašiš. Svaki dan su ga uvjeravali da je marihuana prirodna biljka koja je dobra za zdravlje: razvija mozak, popravlja san i apetit, ne izaziva agresiju ni krizu i ne stvara ovisnost.

Na kraju je probao. Idućih deset dana nije pušio i ponosno je zaključio da je „čovjek od karaktera“ i da svi lažu kad govore o opasnosti. Nakon deset dana zapalio je ponovno, a uskoro je **pušio od jutra do mraka, svaki dan**.

Jednog se dana probudio u bolnici, razbijene i krvave glave. Liječnici su postavili dijagnozu: **epilepsija grand mal**. Bolesti se stidio i zapao je u još težu depresiju. Znao je da mora promijeniti život, ali nije znao kako: otac je bio na brodu, brat svaki dan pijan, a maćeha ga se bojala jer je prema njoj bio agresivan i za sve krivio nju.

S gorkom ironijom zahvaljuje Bogu na „prijateljima“ koji su ga nagovorili na **heroin**, uz obećanje da će njime riješiti sve probleme. Bio je uvjeren da gore ne može biti. Prvi doživljaj euforije opisuje kao „super“. U početku je trebao malo novca za malo heroina, ali potrebe su brzo rasle. Počeo je **krasti automobile, provaljivati u kuće, stanove i restorane te krasti novčanike**, radio je stvari za koje je bio siguran da ih nikad neće raditi.

Ističe i paradoks: otac je cijeli život zarađivao i donosio stvari u kuću, a Goran je **za samo mjesec dana sve pokrao i prodao**. Oca je uhvatila panika.
sections.subtitle_en: "Harmless" Weed, Epilepsy, and Heroin
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran ironically recounts how his friends persuaded him into marijuana
sections.content_en:
After leaving the hospital, along with alcohol Goran also began taking pills. He always hung out with older people, and they had already been smoking marijuana and hashish for a long time. Every day they persuaded him that marijuana is a natural plant that is good for health: it develops the brain, improves sleep and appetite, does not cause aggression or withdrawal, and does not create addiction.

In the end he tried it. For the next ten days he did not smoke and proudly concluded that he was a "man of character" and that everyone was lying when talking about danger. After ten days he lit up again, and soon **he was smoking from morning till night, every day**.

One day he woke up in the hospital, his head smashed and bloody. The doctors made a diagnosis: **grand mal epilepsy**. He was ashamed of the illness and fell into an even more severe depression. He knew he had to change his life, but he did not know how: his father was on the ship, his brother drunk every day, and his stepmother was afraid of him because he was aggressive toward her and blamed her for everything.

With bitter irony he thanks God for the "friends" who talked him into **heroin**, with the promise that with it he would solve all problems. He was convinced that it could not get worse. He describes the first experience of euphoria as "super." In the beginning he needed a little money for a little heroin, but the needs grew quickly. He began **stealing cars, breaking into houses, apartments, and restaurants, and stealing wallets**, doing things he was certain he would never do.

He also points out a paradox: his father had worked and brought things into the house his whole life, and Goran **in just one month stole and sold everything**. Panic seized his father.

sections.subtitle: „Čekam te već 20 godina“: zatvor i psihijatrija kao godišnji odmor
sections.screenshot_description: Goran prepričava očev zakašnjeli poziv na razgovor
sections.content:
Jednog je dana otac u suzama pozvao Gorana: „Gorane, sine, imaš velikih problema. Ajde, sjedi, idemo razgovarati, ja ti hoću pomoći.“ Goran mu je odgovorio da ga čeka **već dvadeset godina** i da je sada kasno.

Bile su to osamdesete, vrijeme komunizma, kada nije bilo centara, savjetovališta ni zajednica. Otac nije znao gdje potražiti pomoć pa je otišao na policiju. Jednog su jutra policajci ušli u Goranovu sobu, bacili mu heroin pokraj glave i proglasili ga dilerom. Goran objašnjava da su mu htjeli pomoći: ako ga zatvore pet-šest mjeseci, možda će shvatiti da je na krivom putu.

Dogodilo se suprotno. U zatvoru je naučio **kako bolje krasti i kako miješati drogu da je ima više**. Droge, alkohola i tableta bilo je jednako kao vani. Izašao je „pametniji nego što je ušao“, a zatvor mu je, kaže, napravio sto puta gore.

Otac je nastavio tražiti pomoć. Jedan njegov prijatelj rekao mu je: „Marko, tvoj sin Goran je bolestan“ i savjetovao da ga se smjesti na psihijatriju jer mu „nitko ne može pomoći nego doktori“. Obitelj je bila sretna. Goran nije htio ići, ali zbog problema sa sudom i policijom morao je. Dva dana prije prijema sve je organizirao.

Psihijatrija u Splitu bila je u prizemlju. Imao je svoj krevet, cijeli dan gledao televiziju i šalio se s pacijentima, liječnici su mu davali tablete, a prijatelji su mu svaki dan **kroz prozor dobacivali drogu i alkohol**. Bilo mu je „kao na godišnjem odmoru“. Jedne je večeri u pidžami s natpisom psihijatrije pobjegao u diskoteku, gdje je plesao i opijao se, dok ga policija nije pretukla i vratila. Liječnici nisu znali što bi s njim jer je remetio sve, pa su ga na kraju izbacili. Kod kuće je nastao pakao: svaki dan policija, hitna pomoć, tučnjave i pijani brat.
sections.subtitle_en: "I Have Been Waiting for You for 20 Years": Prison and Psychiatry as a Vacation
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran recounts his father's belated invitation to talk
sections.content_en:
One day his father called Goran in tears: "Goran, son, you have big problems. Come on, sit down, let's talk, I want to help you." Goran answered him that he had been waiting for him **for twenty years already** and that now it was too late.

Those were the eighties, the time of communism, when there were no centers, counseling services, or communities. His father did not know where to seek help, so he went to the police. One morning police officers entered Goran's room, threw heroin beside his head, and proclaimed him a dealer. Goran explains that they wanted to help him: if they locked him up for five or six months, maybe he would realize that he was on the wrong path.

The opposite happened. In prison he learned **how to steal better and how to mix drugs so there would be more**. There were just as many drugs, alcohol, and pills as outside. He came out "smarter than he went in," and prison, he says, made him a hundred times worse.

His father continued to seek help. A friend of his told him: "Marko, your son Goran is sick" and advised that he be placed in psychiatry because "no one can help him but doctors." The family was happy. Goran did not want to go, but because of problems with the court and the police he had to. Two days before admission, he organized everything.

Psychiatry in Split was on the ground floor. He had his bed, watched television all day and joked with patients, the doctors gave him pills, and his friends **threw drugs and alcohol to him through the window** every day. To him it was "like on vacation." One evening, in pajamas with the psychiatry's inscription, he escaped to a disco, where he danced and got drunk until the police beat him and brought him back. The doctors did not know what to do with him because he disrupted everything, so in the end they kicked him out. At home hell broke loose: every day police, emergency medical service, fights, and a drunk brother.

sections.subtitle: Posao u skladištu, nož na šefa i nož u očev trbuh
sections.screenshot_description: Goran opisuje sukob s ocem koji je završio ubodom nožem
sections.content:
Otac je, kao roditelj, htio pružiti sinu još jednu priliku. Drugi mu je prijatelj savjetovao: „Marko, Goranu trebaš naći posao.“ Računica je opet bila logična: Goran će ustajati rano, raditi osam sati, umoriti se i neće imati ni volje ni vremena za gluposti.

Goran nije htio raditi jer mu je bilo lakše krasti. Tada se okupila cijela rodbina i dala mu ultimátum: **„Radi ili na ulicu.“** Od dva zla izabrao je manje i pristao raditi.

Otac mu je našao posao u skladištu firme u kojoj je i sam radio, sa svime potrebnim za mornare i brodove. Ondje su radili očevi prijatelji, koji su obećali da će se pobrinuti za njega, ako treba ga i istući, i dati mu toliko posla „da će mu se pariti iz ušiju“. Goran to naziva **najvećom očevom pogreškom**. Pokrao je pola skladišta, prodao sve što se moglo prodati i posuđivao novac koji nikome nije vraćao. Jednog se dana naljutio na šefa i **jurio ga nožem po skladištu**. Odmah je dobio otkaz.

Zatim je došao kraj. Pijan i u krizi, tražio je od oca novac. Otac ga je udario šakom u glavu i počeli su se tući. Otac je imao 120 kilograma, a Goran je, vidjevši da će dobiti batine, **uzeo nož i ubo oca u trbuh**. Otac je završio u bolnici, Goran u zatvoru.

I dalje je bio ljut na oca: da mu je dao novac, kupio bi drogu i ništa se ne bi dogodilo. Nakon zatvora htio se vratiti kući kao da se ništa nije dogodilo. Danas kaže da je **potpuni nedostatak savjesti** nešto najgore što se čovjeku može dogoditi. Vrata su bila zaključana, a otac mu je kroz njih rekao: „Između obitelji i ulice, ti si izabrao ulicu. Živi na ulici. Ako odlučiš mijenjati život, dođi, mi ćemo ti pomoći.“ Mržnja je u tom trenutku narasla „milijun puta“. Pljunuo je na vrata, proklinjao i otišao uz riječi da ga otac više nikad neće vidjeti.
sections.subtitle_en: A Job in the Warehouse, a Knife at the Boss, and a Knife in His Father's Stomach
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran describes the conflict with his father that ended with a knife stabbing
sections.content_en:
His father, as a parent, wanted to give his son another chance. Another friend advised him: "Marko, you need to find Goran a job." The logic was again sound: Goran would get up early, work eight hours, get tired, and have neither the will nor the time for foolishness.

Goran did not want to work because it was easier for him to steal. Then the whole extended family gathered and gave him an ultimatum: **"Work or out on the street."** Of two evils he chose the lesser and agreed to work.

His father found him a job in the warehouse of the company where he worked himself, with everything needed for sailors and ships. His father's friends worked there, and they promised that they would take care of him, beat him if necessary, and give him so much work "that steam would come out of his ears." Goran calls this **his father's biggest mistake**. He stole half the warehouse, sold everything that could be sold, and borrowed money that he returned to no one. One day he got angry at his boss and **chased him with a knife around the warehouse**. He was fired immediately.

Then came the end. Drunk and in withdrawal, he asked his father for money. His father hit him with a fist in the head, and they started fighting. His father weighed 120 kilograms, and Goran, seeing that he would get a beating, **took a knife and stabbed his father in the stomach**. His father ended up in the hospital, Goran in prison.

He was still angry with his father: if he had given him the money, he would have bought drugs and nothing would have happened. After prison he wanted to return home as if nothing had happened. Today he says that a **complete lack of conscience** is the worst thing that can happen to a man. The door was locked, and his father told him through it: "Between family and the street, you chose the street. Live on the street. If you decide to change your life, come, we will help you." Hatred at that moment grew "a million times." He spat on the door, cursed, and left with the words that his father would never see him again.

sections.subtitle: Devet godina na ulici, šizofrenija i Popovača u ratu
sections.screenshot_description: Goran govori o dijagnozi šizofrenije i odlasku u Popovaču
sections.content:
Goran je **devet godina živio na ulici kao klošar** i to razdoblje naziva katastrofom. Dok je imao novca i droge, imao je i prijatelja jer je vani sve interes. Došao je do točke kada čak ni tada nitko nije htio biti s njim, toliko je ružno izgledao i nenormalno se ponašao.

Pred kraj života na ulici javili su se **abnormalni strahovi** koje ne može opisati, strahovi „za poluditi, od svega“. Nijedna droga ni tableta nisu ga mogle smiriti. Smirivala ga je samo vlastita krv: rezao se, praznom injekcijom vadio krv, pio je i mazao po sebi.

Kad su ga posljednji put zatvorili, neuropsihijatar u zatvoru postavio je dijagnozu **šizofrenije**. Iz Remetinca je čekao prijevoz na psihijatriju, a tada je počeo rat u Hrvatskoj. Budući da su se prvi kreveti oslobodili na **trećem patološkom odjelu u Popovači**, Goran je s dvojicom mladića završio na odjelu na kojem su bili ubojice. Terapija ga je smirila, ali jednog je jutra za stolom shvatio: „Što ja ovdje radim? Ja sam obični narkoman.“ Bio je uvjeren da će ga ubiti za dva dana, pa je čekao priliku, **ukrao novac kolegi pacijentu i pobjegao**.

U glavi je složio „genijalan“ plan: vratiti se u Split, malo se drogirati, otići u rat, Hrvatska će pobijediti, vlast će se promijeniti i on će biti slobodan. Jednog je jutra ušao u vojarnu i izjavio da kao Hrvat ide braniti državu. Vojnik mu je odgovorio da se okrene i izađe jer će mu slomiti obje noge. Goran se danas tome smije: sada ima 90 kilograma, a tada nije imao ni 60, „sama kost i koža“. Priznaje da bi kalašnjikov, da su mu ga dali, sigurno prodao ili zamijenio za heroin.
sections.subtitle_en: Nine Years on the Street, Schizophrenia, and Popovača During the War
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran talks about the diagnosis of schizophrenia and going to Popovača
sections.content_en:
Goran **lived on the street for nine years as a tramp** and calls that period a catastrophe. While he had money and drugs, he had friends because outside everything is interest. He reached the point where even then no one wanted to be with him, so hideous did he look and so abnormally did he behave.

Toward the end of life on the street, **abnormal fears** arose that he cannot describe, fears "to drive you crazy, of everything." No drug or pill could calm him down. Only his own blood calmed him down: he cut himself, drew blood with an empty syringe, drank it, and smeared it on himself.

When they locked him up for the last time, the neuropsychiatrist in prison made a diagnosis of **schizophrenia**. From Remetinec he waited for transport to psychiatry, and at that time the war in Croatia began. Since the first beds opened up in the **third pathological ward in Popovača**, Goran ended up with two young men in the ward where murderers were kept. The therapy calmed him down, but one morning at the table he realized: "What am I doing here? I am an ordinary junkie." He was convinced that they would kill him in two days, so he waited for an opportunity, **stole money from a fellow patient, and escaped**.

In his head he put together an "ingenious" plan: return to Split, take a few drugs, go to war, Croatia will win, the government will change, and he will be free. One morning he entered a barracks and stated that as a Croat he was going to defend the country. A soldier replied to him to turn around and get out because he would break both of his legs. Goran laughs at that today: now he weighs 90 kilograms, and back then he didn't even weigh 60, "pure skin and bone." He admits that if they had given him a Kalashnikov, he surely would have sold it or traded it for heroin.

sections.subtitle: Pet dana pod pogledom ubojice i neočekivano prijateljstvo
sections.screenshot_description: Goran opisuje pet dana zavezan u sobi s pacijentom kojemu je ukrao novac
sections.content:
Policija je raspisala tjeralicu i Goran je ubrzo uhvaćen te vraćen u Popovaču. Dvojicu tehničara, **Besima i Rifata**, kaže, nikad neće zaboraviti. Pretukli su ga, stavili mu luđačku košulju i zavezali noge za šipke kreveta, „kao zagrebačku salamu“.

Namjerno su ga, kako bi ga kaznili, smjestili u sobu s pacijentom kojemu je ukrao novac, čovjekom koji je **ubio četvero ljudi**. Goran mu je novac uzeo upravo zato što je bio siguran da se nikad neće vratiti. Pet dana taj je čovjek sjedio na krevetu nasuprot njemu, pušio i gledao ga u oči, ne izgovorivši ni riječ. To ga je psihički uništavalo. Svaki put kad bi se čovjek ustao, Goran je mislio da je kraj.

Peti dan čovjek je progovorio: „Ti znaš tko sam ja, što sam napravio i što mogu napraviti.“ Priznao je da je pet dana razmišljao hoće li ga zadaviti, a onda dodao: „Kad si imao hrabrosti meni ukrasti novac, svaka ti čast.“ Goran to naziva „najljepšim trenutkom u životu“. Postali su **najbolji prijatelji**, a za Dragu kaže da je bio dobar.

O Popovači bi, kaže, mogao napisati knjigu. Sve je funkcioniralo dok je bilo lijekova, ali u ratu ih često nije bilo, a zamjene su bile slabe i nastajao je „cirkus“. Ipak, bilo je i lijepih dana.

Pri izlasku pozvao ga je glavni liječnik, **primarijus Milivoj Koludrović**, i upozorio ga: ako počini još jedno kazneno djelo, osobno će ga vratiti i ondje će umrijeti. Goran je odlučio promijeniti život. Vratio se u Split, a prva vrata na koja je pokucao bila su **vrata dilera**. Već sljedećeg popodneva vratio se na staro.
sections.subtitle_en: Five Days Under a Murderer's Gaze and an Unexpected Friendship
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran describes five days tied up in a room with the patient from whom he had stolen money
sections.content_en:
The police issued a warrant and Goran was soon caught and returned to Popovača. The two technicians, **Besim and Rifat**, he says, he will never forget. They beat him, put him in a straitjacket, and tied his legs to the bed bars, "like a Zagreb salami."

Deliberately, in order to punish him, they placed him in a room with the patient from whom he had stolen money, a man who had **killed four people**. Goran had taken his money precisely because he was sure he would never return. For five days that man sat on the bed opposite him, smoked, and looked him in the eyes, without uttering a word. That was destroying him mentally. Every time the man stood up, Goran thought it was the end.

On the fifth day the man spoke: "You know who I am, what I did, and what I can do." He admitted that for five days he had been thinking about whether to strangle him, and then added: "Since you had the guts to steal money from me, kudos to you." Goran calls that the "most beautiful moment in life." They became **best friends**, and about Drago he says that he was good.

About Popovača, he says, he could write a book. Everything functioned while there were medications, but during the war they were often unavailable, and the substitutes were weak and a "circus" ensued. Still, there were also beautiful days.

Upon leaving, the chief physician, **Chief Physician Milivoj Koludrović**, called him in and warned him: if he commits one more criminal offense, he will personally bring him back and he will die there. Goran decided to change his life. He returned to Split, and the first door he knocked on was **the dealer's door**. By the very next afternoon he returned to his old ways.

sections.subtitle: Najdublje dno: kad je smrt izgledala kao spas
sections.screenshot_description: Goran govori o preziru prolaznika i želji za smrću
sections.content:
Goran više nije mogao spavati. Jedan sendvič nosio bi u džepu po dvadeset dana ili mjesec dana i to mu je bila sva hrana. Bio je **pun živih otvorenih rana** i širio je smrad koji, kaže, slušatelji ne mogu ni zamisliti. Kad bi ušao u gradski autobus, svi bi na sljedećoj stanici izašli, pa je uvijek imao gdje sjesti.

Sjedio bi skupljen na zidu, a prolaznici su ga pljuvali, tukli šakama i nogama te vikali da ga treba ubiti jer je **„otrov za djecu“**. Njemu je bilo svejedno. Čekao je samo smrt jer mu je **smrt bila spas, a život samo patnja**. Bezbroj puta popio bi bocu votke i kutiju tableta te se nabo heroinom i po nekoliko dana ležao u komi, ali uvijek bi se probudio. Jednom se ljeti probudio s ustima punima mušica i mrava.

Kad su mu rekli da se žile režu po dužini, na zemlji je pronašao stari žilet. Bio je hrđav i prljav, pa ga je, uz crni humor, „dezinficirao“ pljuvačkom jer se bojao infekcije: „Ako ću već umirati, umrijet ću zdrav.“ Sjedeći na klupi, zarezao je lijevu ruku i otvorio ranu u koju je mogao gurnuti šaku. Dok je krv tekla, pomislio je samo: **„Hvala ti, Isuse, više je gotovo.“** Onesvijestio se i probudio u bolnici. „Koji jadnik, ne može se ni ubiti“, komentira.
sections.subtitle_en: Rock Bottom: When Death Looked Like Salvation
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran speaks about the contempt of passersby and the desire for death
sections.content_en:
Goran could no longer sleep. He would carry a single sandwich in his pocket for twenty days or a month, and that was all his food. He was **full of live open wounds** and emitted a stench that, he says, listeners cannot even imagine. When he would enter a city bus, everyone would get off at the next stop, so he always had a place to sit.

He would sit huddled against a wall, and passersby spat on him, beat him with fists and feet, and shouted that he should be killed because he was **"poison for children."** To him it was all the same. He waited only for death because to him **death was salvation, and life was only suffering**. Countless times he would drink a bottle of vodka and a box of pills and shoot up with heroin and lie in a coma for several days, but he would always wake up. Once in the summer he woke up with his mouth full of flies and ants.

When they told him that veins are cut lengthwise, he found an old razor blade on the ground. It was rusty and dirty, so, with dark humor, he "disinfected" it with spit because he was afraid of infection: "If I'm going to die anyway, I'll die healthy." Sitting on a bench, he cut into his left arm and opened a wound into which he could push his fist. As the blood flowed, he thought only: **"Thank You, Jesus, it is finally over."** He passed out and woke up in the hospital. "What a wretched guy, he can't even kill himself," he comments.

sections.subtitle: Noć u polusrušenoj kućici i molitva Zdravo Marijo
sections.screenshot_description: Goran opisuje trenutak kad je shvatio da je on sam kriv za svoj život
sections.content:
Jedne veljačke večeri Goran je ležao u polusrušenoj kućici, „kao pas na komadu kartona“, uz malu upaljenu svijeću. Počeo je razmišljati o obitelji i djetinjstvu, a što je više razmišljao, to ga je jače boljelo u prsima.

Na kraju je došao do ključne spoznaje: **nitko nije kriv, glavni krivac za sve je on sam**. Cijeli je život krivio druge, najviše obitelj, jer je morao kriviti druge kako bi opravdao zlo koje čini. Kad je shvatio da je on taj koji je sam sebi uništio život, počeo je plakati i moliti **Zdravo Marijo**.

Naglašava koliko je dotad mrzio Boga, Isusa, Gospu, Crkvu, svećenike i vjernike, tolikom mržnjom da je slušatelji ne mogu zamisliti. Zdravo Marijo bila je jedina molitva koja mu je ostala u sjećanju s vjeronauka na koji su ga roditelji tjerali. Cijelu je noć plakao i molio: „Gospe moja, uzmi me gore sebi ili mi pruži ruku da promijenim ovaj bijedni život. **Ja više ne mogu, umoran sam**, radi od mene što god hoćeš.“
sections.subtitle_en: A Night in a Semi-Ruined Shack and the Hail Mary Prayer
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran describes the moment when he realized that he himself was to blame for his life
sections.content_en:
One February evening Goran was lying in a semi-ruined shack, "like a dog on a piece of cardboard," beside a small lit candle. He began thinking about his family and childhood, and the more he thought, the more intensely it hurt in his chest.

In the end he came to a crucial realization: **no one is to blame, the main culprit for everything is he himself**. His whole life he blamed others, most of all his family, because he had to blame others to justify the evil he was doing. When he realized that he was the one who had destroyed his own life, he began to weep and pray the **Hail Mary**.

He emphasizes how much until then he had hated God, Jesus, Our Lady, the Church, priests, and believers, with such hatred that listeners cannot imagine it. The Hail Mary was the only prayer that remained in his memory from the catechism his parents had forced him to attend. All night he wept and prayed: "My Lady, take me up to yourself or extend your hand to me to change this wretched life. **I can't take it anymore, I am tired**, do with me whatever you want."

sections.subtitle: Žena u parku koja je tražila „Čuku“
sections.screenshot_description: Goran prepričava susret sa ženom koja mu je u parku prišla s „problemom“
sections.content:
Nekoliko dana kasnije, rano jednog zimskog jutra, Goran je sjedio skupljen na klupi u parku kad je u park ušla žena i uputila se ravno prema njemu. Uz smijeh publike naglašava da „to nije bila Gospa“. Pozdravila ga je i zamolila za pomoć jer ima „jedan problem“. Goran se razbjesnio: zar ona njemu govori o problemu kad on ima toliko svojih? Grubo ju je otjerao.

Žena je tada rekla da traži mladića kojeg zovu **Čuke**, a to je bio Goranov nadimak na ulici. Bojao se da će, ako prizna, početi vikati, okupiti ljude i pozvati policiju, ali ga je svladala radoznalost. Kad je rekao „Ja sam“, žena je podigla glavu: „O, Gospe moja, hvala ti da sam ga našla.“ Goran je pomislio da nije normalna.

Uhvatila ga je pod ruku i pozvala u šetnju. Pristao je samo zato što je računao da će mu, kad ga već treba, dati novac, i dala mu ga je.

Tada je ispričala svoju priču. Majka je narkomana koji je završio u zatvoru i preko suda je izborila da sin kaznu služi u zajednici koju Goran naziva Černakolo. Pitala je sina ima li prijatelja kojemu bi mogla pomoći, a on je spomenuo Gorana. Goran ističe da u tome **nema nikakve logike**: mladić je deset godina mlađi od njega i s njim je samo dvaput uzeo heroin u jednoj drvarnici.

Žena, **Dijana**, u kratkom mu je vremenu izvadila osobnu iskaznicu i domovnicu jer nije imao nikakvih dokumenata. Zatim ga je odvela na autobusni kolodvor u Splitu i kupila mu kartu. Kad ju je upitao kamo ide, sretno je odgovorila: **„Gorane, ti ideš u Međugorje.“** Objasnila mu je da je to malo mjesto u Bosni i Hercegovini gdje se ukazuje Gospa, koja ga čeka, voli i pomoći će mu. Goran je pomislio: „Ja sam šizofreničar, ali ova je luđa od mene sto puta.“ Ipak je zaključio da je put besplatan, da je klošar može spavati bilo gdje i da je Međugorje udaljeno svega 150-ak kilometara, pa je krenuo „na izlet“.
sections.subtitle_en: The Woman in the Park Who Was Looking for "Čuke"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran recounts the encounter with the woman who approached him in the park with a "problem"
sections.content_en:
A few days later, early one winter morning, Goran was sitting huddled on a bench in the park when a woman entered the park and headed straight toward him. To the laughter of the audience, he emphasizes that "it wasn't Our Lady." She greeted him and asked for help because she had "a problem." Goran became furious: is she talking to him about a problem when he has so many of his own? He rudely chased her away.

The woman then said she was looking for a young man called **Čuke**, which was Goran's nickname on the street. He was afraid that, if he admitted it, she would start screaming, gather people, and call the police, but curiosity overcame him. When he said "It's me," the woman raised her head: "Oh, my Lady, thank you that I found him." Goran thought she was out of her mind.

She took him by the arm and invited him for a walk. He agreed only because he calculated that, since she needed him, she would give him money, and she did give it to him.

Then she told her story. She was the mother of a drug addict who had ended up in prison, and through the court she had fought for her son to serve his sentence in a community that Goran calls Černakolo. She asked her son if he had a friend whom she could help, and he mentioned Goran. Goran emphasizes that **there is no logic in that**: the young man was ten years younger than him and had only twice taken heroin with him in a woodshed.

The woman, **Dijana**, in a short time obtained an identity card and certificate of citizenship for him because he had no documents at all. Then she took him to the bus station in Split and bought him a ticket. When he asked her where he was going, she happily replied: **"Goran, you are going to Međugorje."** She explained to him that it is a small town in Bosnia and Herzegovina where Our Lady appears, who is waiting for him, loves him, and will help him. Goran thought: "I'm a schizophrenic, but this woman is a hundred times crazier than me." Still, he concluded that the trip was free, that as a tramp he could sleep anywhere, and that Međugorje was only about 150 kilometers away, so he set off "on a trip."

sections.subtitle: Ulazak u zajednicu usred krize i otpor prema krunicama
sections.screenshot_description: Goran opisuje svoju reakciju na svakodnevnu molitvu tri krunice u zajednici
sections.content:
Čim je izašao iz autobusa u Međugorju, Goran je u prvom dućanu **ukrao dvije litre vina** i popio ih. Lutajući mjestom došao je do kapije zajednice i sjetio se da mu je Dijana govorila o njoj. Mladići su ga primijetili, razgovarali s njim i odmah ga primili. To naziva čudom jer, kako kaže, **u zajednicu nitko nikad nije ušao u krizi**, a on jest, ni sam ne zna zašto.

Prvi mjesec apstinencijske krize bio je „nešto najgore u životu“: bez tableta, alkohola, cigareta, novina i televizije, samo težak rad i molitva. Mislio je da će umrijeti, no od krize, ističe, nitko nije umro. Odjeću koju su skinuli s njega nije bilo moguće oprati pa su je spalili. **Sestra Elvira** uplašila se, vidjevši ga punog otvorenih rana, da je u posljednjem stadiju side. Odmah su mu napravili sve pretrage i, „Bogu hvala“, nije bio zaražen. Kriza je prošla i polako je dolazio k sebi.

Najviše su ga živcirale **tri krunice koje se u zajednici mole svaki dan**. Govorio je da neće biti svećenik i da nema problem s molitvom, nego s alkoholom, drogom i tabletama. Kad ga je jedan mladić upitao hoće li moliti ili ne, nije htio biti bezobrazan prema onima koji su ga primili. Pristao je na jednu krunicu od 15 do 20 minuta, ali ne na tri. Mladići su odgovorili da će ostale dvije moliti oni za njega, što je on zadovoljno prihvatio. „Cijeli život mi je bio logičan, zato sam i završio gdje sam završio“, zaključuje uz smijeh.
sections.subtitle_en: Entering the Community in the Midst of Withdrawal and Resistance to Rosaries
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran describes his reaction to the daily prayer of three Rosaries in the community
sections.content_en:
As soon as he got off the bus in Međugorje, Goran **stole two liters of wine** in the first store and drank them. Wandering through the town, he came to the gate of the community and remembered that Dijana had spoken to him about it. The young men noticed him, talked with him, and took him in immediately. He calls that a miracle because, as he says, **no one ever entered the community in withdrawal**, but he did, without even knowing why himself.

The first month of withdrawal was "the worst thing in life": without pills, alcohol, cigarettes, newspapers, and television, only hard work and prayer. He thought he was going to die, but from withdrawal, he points out, no one has died. The clothes they took off him were impossible to wash, so they burned them. **Sister Elvira** was frightened, seeing him full of open wounds, that he was in the final stage of AIDS. They immediately ran all tests on him and, "thank God," he was not infected. The withdrawal passed and he slowly came to his senses.

What irritated him most were the **three Rosaries that are prayed in the community every day**. He said that he was not going to be a priest and that he did not have a problem with prayer, but with alcohol, drugs, and pills. When one young man asked him whether he would pray or not, he did not want to be rude to those who had taken him in. He agreed to one Rosary of 15 to 20 minutes, but not to three. The young men answered that they would pray the other two for him, which he gladly accepted. "My whole life was logical, that's why I ended up where I ended up," he concludes with laughter.

sections.subtitle: Lekcija iz kamenoloma: djela, a ne riječi
sections.screenshot_description: Goran opisuje kako je sjedio u hladu dok su drugi za njega razbijali kamen
sections.content:
Goran zatim iznosi priču koju, kaže, nikome nije ispričao desetak godina. Bilo je ljeto, u Međugorju zna biti i 40 do 45 stupnjeva, a odgovorni u zajednici dao mu je **macolu od dvanaest kilograma** i poslao ga u kamenolom. Goran je odbio jer, kako je rekao, nije došao uništiti zdravlje.

Odgovorni mu je rekao da uzme stolicu i sjedne. Drugi mladić dodao je: „Ako ti nećeš raditi, mi ćemo raditi za tebe.“ Goran ih je nazvao budalama. Sjedio je u hladu na plastičnoj stolici, a oni su na žezi u rupi razbijali kamen, dok su im krhotine letjele „kao geleri“ i ranjavale ih. Mislio je da je to gore od koncentracijskog logora.

Nakon nekoliko dana počelo se događati nešto čudno. Mladići su teško radili, ali su bili **sretni: pjevali su, pričali viceve, molili se i šalili**. On nije radio ništa, a bio je ljut, nervozan i ljubomoran, „sve zlo na njemu“. Tada se zapitao tko je zapravo lud, oni koji rade ili on koji ne radi.

Zaključio je da je budala on jer je **prvi put u životu vidio da netko nešto radi za njega**. Shvatio je da u životu često nisu važne riječi, nego djela. Postidio se gledajući kako tovare kamione, ustao je i otišao raditi. Od tada mu se, kaže, život okrenuo.
sections.subtitle_en: A Lesson from the Quarry: Deeds, Not Words
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran describes how he sat in the shade while others broke stone for him
sections.content_en:
Goran then shares a story that, he says, he had not told anyone for about ten years. It was summer, in Međugorje it can be 40 to 45 degrees, and the leader in the community gave him a **twelve-kilogram sledgehammer** and sent him to the quarry. Goran refused because, as he said, he did not come to ruin his health.

The leader told him to take a chair and sit down. Another young man added: "If you won't work, we will work for you." Goran called them fools. He sat in the shade on a plastic chair, and they broke stone in the heat in the pit, while splinters flew "like shrapnel" and wounded them. He thought that was worse than a concentration camp.

After a few days something strange began to happen. The young men worked hard, but they were **happy: they sang, told jokes, prayed, and joked around**. He was doing nothing, yet he was angry, nervous, and jealous, "all evil upon him." Then he wondered who was actually crazy, those who work or he who does not work.

He concluded that he was the fool because **for the first time in his life he saw someone doing something for him**. He realized that in life words are often not important, but deeds. He felt ashamed watching them load the trucks, he stood up and went to work. From then on, he says, his life turned around.

sections.subtitle: Molitva u dva ujutro i zagrljaj oca u blagovaonici
sections.screenshot_description: Goran emotivno prepričava neočekivani susret s ocem i njihov zagrljaj
sections.content:
Nakon jedanaest mjeseci u zajednici u Goranu je rasla **ljubomora koja se pretvarala u mržnju** prema drugim mladićima: njima su dolazile obitelji, a njemu nitko. S obitelji nije imao kontakta deset godina, devet na ulici i godinu u zajednici. Kroz svakodnevnu molitvu savjest mu je ipak sve više rasla. Bilo mu je žao svega što je učinio i htio se pomiriti s obitelji i ocem.

Planirao je napisati pismo, ali su mu mladići rekli da mora prinijeti žrtvu jer **„bez žrtve nema ljubavi i nema plodova“**. Savjetovali su mu da svako jutro ustaje u dva sata, ide u kapelu i ondje sat vremena kleči, moli i vjeruje. Nije mu se dalo, ali je želja za pomirenjem bila jača pa je počeo ustajati, klečati i moliti. Priznaje da nije vjerovao jer je bio siguran da će prije umrijeti nego što će se otac pomiriti s njim.

Nije prošao ni mjesec kada ga je jedan mladić zamolio da hodočasnicima iz Hrvatske pokaže zajednicu. Otvorio je vrata blagovaonice, podigao glavu i prvo lice koje je ugledao bilo je **očevo**. Odmah je spustio pogled. Osjećaj srama i krivnje opisuje kao najteži trenutak u životu i nije imao hrabrosti ponovno pogledati oca. Otac je vidio koliko mu je teško, prišao mu, **zagrlio ga i zaplakao**. Goran je zagrlio njega i oni su cijeli dan samo plakali, bez riječi.

Nije znao što bi rekao. Nije mogao ni tražiti oprost jer nije bio siguran da će uspjeti, a nakon života punog laži prvi je put htio biti pošten i ne davati lažnu nadu. Kad je otac odlazio, rekao mu je da je uništio i sebe i njih, da ne može ništa obećati i da se možda sutra vrati na staru cestu. Zamolio ga je samo za jedno: da sa svojom ženom počne moliti za njegovo obraćenje.

Otac ga je pogledao i odgovorio: **„Sinko, pa mi se već dugo godina za tebe molimo.“** Goran danas smatra da je sve tako trebalo biti kako bi se molitva i vjera vratile u njegovu obitelj. Svatko, kaže, ima svoj križni put kojim mu Bog daje do znanja da se mora vratiti Crkvi, a sva ta patnja i bol imale su smisla.
sections.subtitle_en: Prayer at Two in the Morning and a Father's Embrace in the Dining Hall
sections.screenshot_description_en: Goran emotionally recounts the unexpected encounter with his father and their embrace
sections.content_en:
After eleven months in the community, in Goran grew a **jealousy that turned into hatred** toward the other young men: their families came to visit them, but no one came to him. He had had no contact with his family for ten years, nine on the street and one in the community. Through daily prayer, however, his conscience grew more and more. He was sorry for everything he had done and wanted to reconcile with his family and father.

He planned to write a letter, but the young men told him that he had to offer a sacrifice because **"without sacrifice there is no love and there are no fruits."** They advised him to get up every morning at two o'clock, go to the chapel, and kneel, pray, and believe there for an hour. He didn't feel like it, but the desire for reconciliation was stronger, so he began getting up, kneeling, and praying. He admits that he did not believe because he was sure he would die before his father would reconcile with him.

Not even a month had passed when a young man asked him to show pilgrims from Croatia around the community. He opened the dining hall door, raised his head, and the first face he saw was **his father's**. He immediately lowered his gaze. He describes the feeling of shame and guilt as the hardest moment in his life, and he did not have the courage to look at his father again. His father saw how hard it was for him, approached him, **embraced him, and wept**. Goran embraced him, and they just wept all day, without words.

He did not know what to say. He could not even ask for forgiveness because he was not sure he would succeed, and after a life full of lies, for the first time he wanted to be honest and not give false hope. When his father was leaving, he told him that he had destroyed both himself and them, that he could promise nothing, and that maybe tomorrow he would return to the old path. He asked him for only one thing: to begin praying with his wife for his conversion.

His father looked at him and answered: **"Son, we have already been praying for you for many years."** Goran today believes that everything was meant to be that way so that prayer and faith would return to his family. Everyone, he says, has their own Way of the Cross by which God lets them know that they must return to the Church, and all that suffering and pain had meaning.
